summary: A remote is another copy of the repository, usually on GitHub. git clone downloads one, and git remote lists and adds the names you use to reach them.
notes: Here the remotes are folders on the same computer. With GitHub the URL looks like https://github.com/maya/gradebook.git, and the commands are the same.
origin is only a default name. git remote add gives any URL a name you choose.
A .git ending marks a bare repository: it stores history but has no working files, like the copy on GitHub.
pitfall: Running git clone inside another repository puts one repository inside the other. cd to the folder where you keep projects first.
setup_note: Starts in an empty folder. ../gradebook.git is the class repository with two commits, and ../backup.git is an empty repository.
setup:
cat > gradebook.py <<'EOF'
scores = [88, 92, 79, 95]
average = sum(scores) / len(scores)
print("Average:", average)
EOF

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Gradebook
Quiz scores for Period 3.
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add gradebook script"

cat > scores.csv <<'EOF'
name,score
Ava,88
Liam,92
Noah,79
Zoe,95
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add quiz scores"
